hints.title: Ordered Pair Inspection
hints.text: Both arrays are already sorted in ascending order of identifiers. Compare the front elements of both arrays.

hints.title: Key Matching and Increment
hints.text: If ids match, sum their values and advance both indices. If one id is smaller, append it alone and advance its index.

hints.title: Residual Append
hints.text: When one array is exhausted, append the remaining entries of the other array.

hints.title: Two-Pointer Sorted Merge Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def mergeArrays(self, nums1: list[list[int]], nums2: list[list[int]]) -> list[list[int]]:
        i, j = 0, 0
        n, m = len(nums1), len(nums2)
        res = []
        while i < n and j < m:
            id1, val1 = nums1[i]
            id2, val2 = nums2[j]
            if id1 == id2:
                res.append([id1, val1 + val2])
                i += 1
                j += 1
            elif id1 < id2:
                res.append([id1, val1])
                i += 1
            else:
                res.append([id2, val2])
                j += 1
        while i < n:
            res.append(nums1[i])
            i += 1
        while j < m:
            res.append(nums2[j])
            j += 1
        return res
```

complexity.notes: Linear two-pointer merge over both sorted arrays.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Merging and then sorting takes O((n + m) log(n + m)).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(1) auxiliary space beyond the output list.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Merges two sorted lists in linear time analogous to merge sort.
